_about: Progress tracker data for the README. tools/gen_docs.py turns this into the <!-- gen:progress --> block. Game counts for the newest release come from the live registry; older releases keep the counts they shipped with.

releases.added: Last checks and polish. The five 3D worlds that crashed or timed out in the test browser (Abyss Diver, Storm Royale, Frontline, Starfall, Strike Zone) now pass, and the full test suite passes for every cabinet. Zombie Road is redrawn with a burning city skyline, a proper road and a new truck, Cave Raid gains layered cave walls and glowing crystals, and the Nova Arena guns are no longer near-black.

3D world pass and Rocket Arena polish. All 52 other 3D worlds were played past their menus with random input and checked screen by screen. Bastion Line's diorama now sits on a war-room table instead of floating in empty sky when you pan or turn the camera, and the Longbow Keep bow is a proper tapered bow with a visible string. Rocket Arena gains a floor marker under a high ball for judging aerials and an arrow at the screen edge pointing to the ball when it is off screen.

Clean-up sweep of the other games. Every arcade cabinet was run with random input looking for frozen screens, games that never end and clipped text, and the 3D worlds were played past their menus. Score and bonus pop-ups now always stay on screen instead of drifting off an edge or under the top bar, and the first-person shooter cabinet no longer shows negative health on the death frame. The quality sweep (tests/qa.js) reports each problem as it finds it and can be split across processes.

A slower, clearer front-page intro and new README key art. The scroll intro now tells five short chapters (the games, the 3D worlds, no installs or accounts, the round clock, insert coin), each holding still for about half a screen of scrolling with a sentence of detail, a darkened reading panel and a clickable chapter rail. The README opens on a tilted, drifting wall of 3D world screenshots behind the title instead of a crop of the intro.

Rocket Arena rebuilt: cars are now solid bodies with four wheel probes, so they ride smoothly up ramps, walls and the ceiling and never sink into the floor, walls, posts or goals (worst sink in a 3v3 bot match: under 1 cm, it used to be over a metre). Smoother steering, no speed lost up the curves, a landing assist, quick roof recovery, a wall-aware camera that never hides your car, 2/3/5 minute matches, and an original twist: Overcharge, where three touches in a row by one team ignite the ball and an ignited goal counts double.

More world clean-up: Night Drive gets street trees in iron-grated pavement pits along midtown and downtown, kept clear of lamps, garages, furniture and pedestrians; Neon Bay corner palms no longer cross fronds or cut into shopfronts, and its decorative trees, palms and pines no longer grow inside each other.
Rounds 27 and 28 in one build: the cleaner 3D worlds from v55 (no more trees, rocks, rooftop units and parked cars spawning inside each other) and the colourful cartridges with pixel icons from v56.

Colourful cartridges: every one of the 521 cartridges on the shelf now has its own shell colour (18 bright plastics, never the same twice in a row) and a pixel icon on its label (60 icons, picked from the game's name and tags), in the same cartridge shape. Spines and boxes are bigger, the console tray cartridges match, and the shelf planks line up under every row again.

A clean-up round for the worlds around the player. Trees, rocks, rooftop units, street furniture, parked cars and distant skylines no longer spawn inside each other, on pavements or hanging off roofs, using a new shared placement guard (js/kit3d/place.js). Night Drive, Kart Grand Prix, Sideways, Kart, Courier, Royale, Warfront, Nightfall, Plaza, Drop Zone, Strike, Frontline, Siege and Zenith are cleaner, and Night Drive trees get fuller canopies.

A new README front page: an animated header that drifts through the arcade under light shafts while the middle cabinet flips between real games, a scrolling LED ticker of game names, arcade-button links, a counts strip, and a feature grid of the 3D worlds, cabinets, round clock, CPU levels, builder, online codes and platforms. All of it is drawn by tools/readme_intro.js.

A graphics round for four games that still looked plain. NEON FIGHTERS rebuilt on a rain-soaked neon rooftop with jointed fighters in glowing suits, a wet floor that reflects them, hit-stop, combos, sweeps, knockdowns and four elemental specials you duck or jump; CRATE PUSHER rebuilt as a lamp-lit warehouse with wooden crates, an undo button and three new rooms; GOLF DUEL rebuilt with three themed holes (meadow, canyon, lantern pond), sand, water, bumpers and a smarter CPU; FIRE FIGHTER rebuilt as a street block that turns from dusk to night, with a fire truck, a hose, smoke, steam and fires that spread. The front-page repainted row shows all four.

A graphics round for four classics. BLOCK DROP rebuilt with cut-glass tiles, a sky that changes every level, a hold slot, a three-piece preview, fair seven-piece shuffling, combos and back-to-back bonuses; MUNCH MAZE rebuilt with glowing neon tube walls, four bugs that each hunt differently, bonus fruit and a proper death animation; HELIX DROP rebuilt as a spinning 3D tower whose floors shatter as you drop through, with a fireball that smashes floors after three clean drops; ROAD HOPPER rebuilt with diving turtles, flies to catch, headlights at dusk and a time bonus. The front-page repainted row shows all four.

A new story adventure: XENOSHIFT, a side-scroller in three chapters (a seaside town, glowing caves and a warship in orbit) where a boy's alien band turns him into seven different aliens, each one the key to a different obstacle, with a boss at the end of every chapter. MORPHBAND repainted with bigger fighters, a living aurora, the pod's light beam, ground fog and a DNA-helix transformation. BYTE SNAKE rebuilt as a garden with gliding movement, three fruits, mice to catch and rocks; INVADER WAVE rebuilt with painted aliens that dive at you, a city skyline and a double-cannon power-up. Xenoshift plays in the front-page spotlight.

Two new versus games: HEAT RUN (a night-time getaway through a city full of police, with drifting, nitro, wanted stars and a helicopter) and FLOPPY HOOPS (one-button wobbly basketball, two players a side, with new rules and a new court after every basket). MOON LANDER rebuilt with a camera that zooms in for touchdown, three scored pads, dust and a flag; BRICK BUSTER rebuilt with six brick maps, metal, gold and bomb bricks, lasers, fireballs and combos. Heat Run plays in the front-page spotlight.

Three new hero and space versus games: MORPHBAND (a wrist band that turns you into four different aliens), OVERDRIVE AGENT (an energy suit with four modes, raced through a robot-filled city) and NOVA REBELLION (a starfighter battle, then a light-blade duel on the enemy flagship). TRENCH RUN 3D gets a steel trench, turrets that shoot back and reactor ports to hit; STAR RUN 3D gets lumpy lit asteroids, raider fighters and shield rings. Morphband plays in the front-page spotlight.

Two new versus games, ROOFTOP SCRAMBLE (a wobbly rooftop race to a helicopter ladder, with guns and a moving train) and NEBULA RUN (a race down a tile tunnel floating in deep space), a rebuilt ROCK BLASTER with flying saucers and power-ups, a rebuilt TANK DUEL with ricochet shells, crates and three maps, and Nebula Run in the front-page spotlight.

Two new versus games, SINKHOLE CITY (a growing-hole duel over a city block) and RIDGE RUNNER (a split-screen hill-climb jeep race), smart bombs and mutants in SPACE DEFENDER, painted fruit and a frenzy fruit in FRUIT SLICE, and a new front-page spotlight.

A fully modelled PIXEL ARCADE machine at the heart of the front-page intro, every cabinet rebuilt in detail (printed side art, T-molding, joysticks and buttons, curved CRT screens, coin doors), a dressed arcade room with neon signs, hanging lamps and blacklight carpet, and a graphics pass on 3 games.
MELON DROP, a fruit-merge physics duel with a CPU rival (search "suika"), a New on the shelf spotlight on the front page, and a graphics pass on 22 more games.

Playable cabinets in the front-page intro (point to light one up, click to play), soft light shafts and a pointer spotlight in the 3D room, pointer tilt with light sweeps on the posters and console, and a graphics pass on 38 games (lighting, shadows, parallax, glows and particles).

A scroll-driven front-page intro that flies through the 3D arcade room into a cabinet screen, decoding headings, scroll reveals and a world-name marquee, and a cinematic docs header with a progress bar.

The README header is back as a refurbished 3D ring of arcade cabinets with real game screens under the PIXEL ARCADE title; Big box worlds became a cinema band of posters with a Show all button; a PIXEL ARCADE sign-off with FREE PLAY in the footer.

Cartridge Shelf redesign of the hub and a new docs site: genre shelves of cartridge spines, a box panel for each game, a front-page console with attract mode, a round clock and drag-to-insert, light and dark modes, and the engine's pixel font as a web font.

Realism and depth pass on six more 3D worlds (STRIKER 11 second pass, IRON VANGUARD, STORM ROYALE, WILD QUEST, KART GRAND PRIX, ABYSS DIVER); the new lifeguard surfing world SWELL GUARD; this progress tracker.
Realism and depth pass on six flagship 3D worlds: FRONTLINE OPS, SIDEWAYS, STRIKER 11, DUSTWATER, FAIRWAY LEGENDS, NEON BAY.
Four new 3D worlds from the inspiration pack: BEACON RESCUE, LANTERN STREET, TIDEWAY COURIER, HARBOR PALS.
BASTION LINE and FAIRWAY LEGENDS, a 43-game art pass, cheaper ambient occlusion, COURT KINGS and SILENT CONTRACT polish.
Rounds 1 to 6: repository reorganisation, the shared 3D kit, online play codes, dozens of new 3D worlds and art passes on the canvas cabinets.

realism._about: Realism pass status per 3D world id: the release that shipped it and how many passes it has had. Worlds not listed are still to do.
